transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Derek Wu (Redwood CSM); Marta Gibson (Nimbly Head of ML), Omar Singh (Nimbly Infra), Leah Park (Product Owner)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Goal: finalize POC acceptance criteria and reporting format for the Nimbly Health assistant POC.
- Agreed on set of go/no-go thresholds (latency, accuracy, stability), 3-day validation run + 30-minute spike test, and reporting CSV template.
- Redwood to send bench plan + acceptance spreadsheet; customer to provide eval set.

Topics: success metrics, workload sizing, bench plan, acceptance tests, reporting format, stakeholders and timelines

Action items (captured quickly): see meta action_items above

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)

[00:00] Lucas: Okay, everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — Lucas Rivera, AE. Priya is our SE and will walk through the acceptance criteria portion. Derek from CSM for on-boarding.

[00:10] Marta: Hi all, Marta here. We wanted to lock this down today because legal needs a go/no-go for procurement schedule.

[00:18] Leah: Yep timeline is tight — we want to start integration by mid July so signoff this week would be ideal.

[00:25] Priya: Great. I'll share my screen in a minute. High level — we propose two phases for acceptance: functional correctness + quality (accuracy & hallucination), and performance/stability (latency, throughput, error rate). Is that aligned?

[00:40] Omar: Yep, that sounds right. Quick note on infra: we'll be testing in your hosted mode first, then dedicated if needed. Bandwidth is typical 1G L3 peering, nothing funky.

[00:55] Priya: Perfect. For workload sizing you said production expected at ~120 RPS peak with 512-token average context?

[01:05] Marta: That's our estimation — about 100-150 qps peak, average 480 tokens, 95th percentile 1024 tokens on longer reports. We're trying to emulate user sessions with multi-turn.

[01:15] Lucas: Noted. So acceptance thresholds we propose:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency < 300ms for typical 512-token cases on hosted; for dedicated SLA target p95 < 200ms (we'll note delta due to reserved GPUs).
- Stability: error rate < 0.5% over 72-hour run.
- Quality: pass if > 90% of eval queries meet the rubric (we'll detail rubric).
- Hallucination: < 2% critical hallucination rate on redacted test set.

[01:40] Marta: Two quick pushbacks — first, 300ms p95 seems optimistic for 512 tokens over hosted. Our users expect sub-400ms. Second, 90% quality threshold depends a lot on prompt engineering.

[01:52] Priya: Totally fair. We left some headroom. We can make thresholds configurable per-test. Proposed acceptance is 'green if meets all thresholds; yellow if meets all but one soft threshold (e.g., latency), red if fails quality or hallucination thresholds.'

[02:05] Leah: What about reporting? We need a CSV or JSON weekly export for audit. We also want sample outputs for manual review attached.

[02:12] Priya: We'll produce a reporting CSV with fields: timestamp, test_id, prompt_id, context_tokens, response_tokens, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_flag, model_version, cost_tokens, sample_output_link. Also a separate sheet for qualitative scoring: rubric_score, hallucination_flag, reviewer_notes.

[02:28] Omar: Can you include system metrics — GPU utilization, memory, and CPU? Our infra team wants to make sure no throttling.

[02:34] Priya: Yes, we'll include host metrics aggregated by minute (avg CPU%, GPU%, mem) and attach graphs in the dashboard link.

[02:45] Lucas: On the eval set — Marta, if you can provide 1k rows with expected outputs or golden labels that helps automated scoring. If no golden output, we'll do human review on a stratified sample of 200.

[02:56] Marta: We can provide redacted golden labels for 60% and rest will need human review.

[03:02] Priya: Good — acceptance plan will reflect that mixed scoring approach. For go/no-go we recommend:
- Go: Passes quality and hallucination thresholds AND p95 latency within target (or yellow with agreed mitigation).
- No-go: Fails quality or hallucination OR stability run shows error spikes >0.5% or sustained thundering errors.

[03:20] Speaker 3: (background) noise — but yes agreed.

[03:26] Leah: What about the spike test? You mentioned a 30-minute spike. What are numbers?

[03:30] Priya: We'll run a 30-minute spike to 1.5x expected peak — so ~180 RPS with a mix of short and long contexts. Success is no sustained p95 degradation beyond +30% of baseline and error rate under 1% during spike.

[03:45] Omar: During spike can you throttle batching? We want to see behavior with burst capacity.

[03:49] Priya: We'll test autoscaling/burst behavior. For hosted there's an autoscale policy that adds instances; for dedicated we simulate constrained capacity. We'll capture KV cache hit rates as well.

[04:05] Marta: For quality rubric — can you outline the scoring? Automatic match won't work for free-form.

[04:12] Priya: Our suggested rubric (high level): 0-2 scale per query — 2 = correct & concise, 1 = partially correct or missing minor facts, 0 = incorrect or harmful. We'll compute % >=1 and % ==2. Acceptance wants >=90% >=1 and >=70% ==2 as a sample target; we can adjust to Nimbly's tolerance.

[04:32] Lucas: And hallucination detection — we mark critical hallucination if it invents clinical facts or misattributes treatments. That's a fail condition if >2% in the sample.

[04:45] Leah: Ok that's reasonable. One more on reporting cadence — legal wants daily reports during the 72-hour run and a final consolidated report with CSV + dashboard.

[04:55] Derek: We'll enable daily exports to the shared S3 bucket (or secure transfer) and keep retention for 30 days for audit. We will include a recording of the run and the dashboard snapshot.

[05:10] Marta: KMS requirement — for any PII we need to ensure keys are controlled. For hosted test can we use Redwood-managed KMS but log key usage?

[05:20] Lucas: For the POC test, Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable if logs are exported; for private or production we'd expect customer-managed KMS. We'll include KMS audit logs in the report.

[05:32] Omar: Network — we need to confirm VPC peering and egress IPs. I'll send CIDR and firewall rules after the call.

[05:40] Priya: Great. A few operational details on the bench plan:
- We'll run a baseline 4-hour run with synthetic traffic to establish baseline p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens.
- Then the 72-hour stability run (lower fidelity but realistic mix) with daily snapshot at 24/48/72h.
- Then the 30-minute spike as described.
- We'll capture sample outputs for every 100th request for manual scoring and full logs for automated checks.

[06:10] Marta: How will we handle model rollbacks or fallbacks if we fail?

[06:15] Priya: We'll propose an automatic fallback policy: if latency or errors exceed threshold, route to a lighter model variant or cached responses for top-N queries. We'll document A/B config and rollback runbook in the acceptance spreadsheet.

[06:30] Leah: On pass/fail signoff — who signs? We prefer a simple sign-off matrix: Redwood AE + Nimbly Product + Nimbly ML sign-off. Legal to confirm but that's the working model.

[06:40] Lucas: Fine by us. We'll include a sign-off section in the acceptance doc that lists signatures (electronic ok).

[06:46] Marta: A few gotchas — our dataset has PHI even after redaction, so be careful with logs. We need logs to be scrubbed and access limited.

[06:53] Derek: We'll ensure masking rules on logs and restrict access to named Redwood engineers for the POC. We'll document ACLs.

[07:05] Omar: Any estimated cost for running these tests? We need a budget approval.

[07:10] Lucas: We'll provide a rough estimate in the bench plan. Rough ballpark: the 72-hour stability run on hosted for this workload is estimated at ~ $4-6k depending on model choice and token mix; dedicated has different commit economics. Exact numbers in spreadsheet.

[07:28] Marta: OK please make that explicit line-item so procurement can sign off.

[07:33] Priya: We'll add a cost breakdown: token cost, instance-hours, monitoring add-ons.

[07:40] Speaker 2: (inaudible)

[07:45] Leah: One more question — the reporting CSV, can you include sample_output_link as a signed URL to the S3 object so reviewers can click through?

[07:51] Priya: Yes, we'll include signed URLs valid for 30 days and attach a permanent archived bundle for audit.

[08:00] Lucas: To recap — action items as captured: Redwood sends bench plan and acceptance spreadsheet by 7/1; Nimbly provides eval set and infra details by 7/3; schedule 3-day run week of 7/7; follow-up signoff call 7/10. Anyone see anything missing?

[08:18] Marta: Sounds good. Add golden-output availability as a note — we'll try to deliver as much as we can but expect a 60/40 split.

[08:26] Omar: I'll send firewall/CIDR and the inference script.

[08:30] Leah: I'll coordinate product signoff attendees for 7/10.

[08:34] Derek: I'll set up the dashboard access and the S3 share info.

[08:38] Lucas: Excellent. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and bench runs.

[08:45] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.

[08:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels, background noise at ~03:20 and 07:40, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (KV cache sometimes as "k v cash"), P95 sometimes written as P nine five.

References mentioned: acceptance spreadsheet (will be shared), bench plan doc (will be shared), S3 bucket for reports, dashboard snapshot link (to be provided).

End of transcript.
